answer: Give every agent a hash-chained history: each completed, independently verified job is appended to a chain anchored at the agent's first verified inlet into the economy, so the chain cannot be copied or forked to a new identity. A farm spinning up one more fake must build a whole fresh chain — thirty attested jobs, each checked by unrelated verifiers — before it earns anything. That cost grows with every identity, unlike a flat fee paid once. One umber flaw, a broken link, invalidates the whole history, and no nebula of unverified claims substitutes for it.
